newsitem.title: CHINA: China welcomes Cambodia closure of Taiwan office.
newsitem.headline: China welcomes Cambodia closure of Taiwan office.

text.p: China on Thursday welcomed Cambodia's decision to close down the Phnom Penh representative office of its arch-rival Taiwan.
"We welcome the closure of the Taiwan representative office in Phnom Penh by the Cambodian side," Foreign Ministry spokesman Tang Guoqiang told a regular news briefing.
"We believe the Cambodian side will deal with this matter under the principle of one China," he said, referring to Beijing's stand that the island is a renegade province of China.

Cambodian co-premier Hun Sen decided on Tuesday to close down Taipei's office in Cambodia, alleging it had been involved in backing forces loyal to First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, whom Hun Sen deposed in a coup this month.
Taiwan's foreign ministry on Thursday threatened "drastic measures" against Cambodia if it does not revoke its decision to close Taipei's unofficial trade office.
Taiwan, the largest foreign investor in Cambodia, has categorically denied any involvement by its government or people in the conflict.
Cambodia has no political ties with Taiwan, and recognises communist China, which has regarded the island as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949.
Earlier, Hun Sen said unidentified Taiwanese, including a general, supported Ranariddh's forces before fighting erupted between troops loyal to the two premiers on July 5.
Hun Sen said Beijing's embassy in Phnom Penh was sufficient to look after the interests of Chinese people in Cambodia.
Taiwan said it did not rule out the possibility that Beijing was involved in Hun Sen's decision.
China's Tang did not answer a question on whether Beijing had been involved in Hun Sen's move.
